questions.prompt: A browser restores a page from the back-forward cache. Which event property can distinguish this from an ordinary page load?

choices.text: DOMContentLoaded fires again.
load.persisted is true only after every script has executed again.
pageshow.persisted is true.
beforeunload reports a restore flag after the previous page is destroyed.

questions.explanation: pageshow fires on normal loads and bfcache restores, and persisted identifies a restore. A restoration reuses the page rather than reparsing and rerunning every script.

sources.title: Back/forward cache  |  Articles  |  web.dev
sources.claim: pageshow with persisted true identifies a back-forward cache restoration; page state including the JS heap can be retained.

questions.prompt: An infinite-scroll sentinel crosses an IntersectionObserver threshold. What delivery model should the callback code expect?

choices.text: Synchronous delivery on style changes.
A callback on every animation frame even when no threshold has changed.
A worker-thread callback with direct access to the browser DOM nodes.
Asynchronous observation delivery.

questions.explanation: IntersectionObserver queues observations asynchronously as intersection thresholds change. It is not synchronous layout instrumentation or an every-frame DOM worker API.

sources.title: Intersection Observer
sources.claim: IntersectionObserver delivers asynchronous threshold-crossing observations; it measures intersection rather than proving actual visibility.

questions.prompt: A ResizeObserver callback changes the observed element's width on every notification. Which statements describe this feedback problem? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The callback can cause another size change that needs observation.
The browser can report undelivered notifications when a resize loop is detected.
Observing an element automatically prohibits code from changing its size.
The callback always runs on a worker thread outside browser layout.
A loop error proves the browser has fixed the application's layout logic.

questions.explanation: A is correct: layout writes can feed back into the observed size. B is correct: the processing algorithm limits cycles and reports its loop error. C is incorrect: observation does not make its style or geometry read-only. D is incorrect: ResizeObserver delivery participates in the rendering update processing. E is incorrect: the browser limits delivery but does not repair a recurring application loop.

sources.title: Resize Observer
sources.claim: ResizeObserver reports box-size changes and can detect resize feedback loops; deferring expected layout mutations can break same-cycle loops.

sources.title: ResizeObserver - Web APIs | MDN
sources.claim: Resize feedback may produce loop errors; requestAnimationFrame defers resizing, while expected-size checks prevent repeated changes.

questions.prompt: A dashboard resumes from the browser back-forward cache with old account data in memory. What is a suitable place to refresh sensitive or stale state on restoration?

choices.text: Handle pageshow when persisted is true.
Rely on DOMContentLoaded running again.
Assume the browser rebuilt the JavaScript heap from a fresh document.
Wait for beforeunload to fire after the restored page becomes visible.

questions.explanation: A bfcache restore can preserve heap state and does not rerun the ordinary load pipeline. The pageshow restoration signal can trigger necessary state refresh.

sources.title: Back/forward cache  |  Articles  |  web.dev
sources.claim: pageshow with persisted true identifies a back-forward cache restoration; page state including the JS heap can be retained.

questions.prompt: A sentinel is geometrically intersecting the viewport but covered by another element. What does ordinary IntersectionObserver intersection establish?

choices.text: Guaranteed unobscured pixels.
Geometric intersection, not guaranteed visibility.
That the user has already seen and read the content inside the sentinel.
That pointer events will reach the sentinel before any overlapping element.

questions.explanation: Ordinary intersection information is geometric. It does not establish that overlapping content, opacity or user attention permits actual visibility.

sources.title: Intersection Observer
sources.claim: IntersectionObserver delivers asynchronous threshold-crossing observations; it measures intersection rather than proving actual visibility.

questions.prompt: A component needs to respond to observed size without endlessly resizing itself. Which design statements are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Box-size observations concern geometry rather than user attention.
ResizeObserver fires only when the browser window is resized.
Deferring a perpetually growing width makes the growth terminate automatically.
Avoiding a write when the target size is already reached can stop feedback.
Scheduling a needed write for a later animation frame can avoid same-cycle feedback.

questions.explanation: A is correct: ResizeObserver observes element box dimensions. B is incorrect: element sizes can change independently of the window. C is incorrect: deferral can shift the loop across frames but an unbounded growth rule still needs correction. D is correct: idempotent size handling avoids repeating an unnecessary geometry change. E is correct: deferring mutations separates the observer delivery from that write cycle.
